title: Pushforward of quasi-coherent modules
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes. Then $f_*$ transforms quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules
into quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules.
(*Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma 26.24.1, Tag
[01LC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LC).*)

proof.text: Apply the existing principal-open quasi-coherence criterion to f_*F. Fix an affine open W of S and a section a of O_S on W. By quasi-compactness of f, V=f^{-1}W is quasi-compact. By quasi-separatedness of f and affineness of W, V is quasi-separated. In Lean these two statements are f.isCompact_preimage hW.isCompact and f.isQuasiSeparated_preimage hW.isQuasiSeparated. Also f^{-1}D_W(a)=D_V(f.app W a), by f.preimage_basicOpen.

For a section s of f_*F on D_W(a), identify it with a section of F on D_V(f.app W a). Apply the qcqs-open section-extension theorem to obtain n and t on V whose restriction is (f.app W a)^n times s. Naturality of the scheme structure map identifies the restricted scalar with the pullback of a|D_W(a); the scalar action in pushforward is restriction of scalars. Thus t is the extension required by the first condition of the criterion.

For a section t of f_*F on W vanishing on D_W(a), identify it with a section on V vanishing on D_V(f.app W a). The compact-open power-torsion theorem gives (f.app W a)^n t=0. By the scalar action of pushforward this is a^n t=0, the second condition of the criterion. The existing criterion now gives quasi-coherence of f_*F.
